subject.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets

question: Should OpenClaw disable `ws` 8.21 retained-part limits entirely for trusted Discord gateway sockets while relying on the existing 16 MiB `maxPayload` cap?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and supported by dependency evidence, but it removes a dependency-level hardening check on a live network path, which is a maintainer security and availability tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Discord-only disable
options.body: Merge after exact-head validation if maintainers accept Discord as a trusted peer and `maxPayload` as the byte-size guard for this route.

options.title: Require finite caps
options.body: Ask for production-informed nonzero `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` values plus proof that they still survive the reported Discord gateway traffic.

options.title: Use alternate mitigation
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer a temporary `ws` pin, upstream fix, or broader Discord gateway transport strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept Discord-only disable
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head validation if maintainers accept Discord as a trusted peer and `maxPayload` as the byte-size guard for this route.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to this account and recent history shows ownership around the affected Discord gateway diagnostics and proxy path.
